ops.text:
CORRECTION to "ccx vcs ship hangs after staging": it is not a hang, it is a slow hook run with zero visibility

Root-caused 2026-08-28 by reproducing it in a scratch clone and taking a SIGQUIT goroutine dump. The earlier papercut called this a hang/deadlock. That was wrong, and the wrong diagnosis pointed at the wrong fix.

Actual stack at the time of the apparent hang:
  runShip (ship.go:351) -> shipCommitLocal (:525) -> shipCommit (:558)
    -> shipRunHooks (ship_hooks.go:86) -> shipRunPrek (:123)
      -> render.RunCLIStream -> RunCLIStreamSplitEnv (render.go:166) -> cmd.Run

Process tree underneath: ccx -> uv tool uvx -> prek run -> golangci-lint. So ccx was correctly blocked on a child that was genuinely still working.

Three facts that together produce "it looks hung":
1. `uvx prek run` over this repo takes ~4 minutes wall (measured: 3:53 for two files), dominated by golangci-lint on a cold cache.
2. shipRunHooks runs prek TWICE on a nonzero first pass -- the auto-fix-then-verify policy -- so a failing suite costs ~8 minutes.
3. Off a terminal, shipStreamCI(errW) is false, so the first pass's writer is nil and RunCLIStream discards everything. The caller sees no output at all for those minutes.

Not implicated, checked and ruled out: cmd.WaitDelay is already set to 5s in newCmd (render.go:52), so a descendant holding the inherited pipes is not the cause. findCIRuns is bounded by shipCIPollTries, not an unbounded poll.

Why the first pass failed at all, making it run twice: prek's golangci-lint hook env ships no Go of its own and runs the ambient one under GOTOOLCHAIN=local. mise's global `go = "latest"` had resolved to 1.26.5 while go.mod requires >= 1.26.6, so every golangci-lint invocation died with "go.mod requires go >= 1.26.6 (running go 1.26.5; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)". The local lint gate was therefore not merely slow, it was non-functional.

Fixes applied:
- mise.toml now pins `[tools] go` to match go.mod's directive, so the ambient toolchain satisfies GOTOOLCHAIN=local.
- ship_hooks.go announces the hook run when it is not streaming, so a slow suite is distinguishable from a hang.
- The post-auto-fix failure message now states that nothing was committed and the working copy is left staged, because finishing that commit by hand skips the checks -- which is exactly what happened and put two gosec findings into CI.

Still open: ~4 minutes for a two-file prek run is itself worth attacking; the auto-fix-then-verify policy doubles it.
